definition: Skewness is a statistical measure of how unevenly values are distributed around the center of a dataset. In research methods, it is used when checking whether data follow a normal distribution, since marked skewness can indicate that normality assumptions are violated.

reasons: The packet does not define skewness as “a statistical measure of how unevenly values are distributed around the center of a dataset.”

While the packet mentions using standardized scores of “skewness” (with kurtosis) and the Shapiro-Wilk test to assess violated assumptions of normality, it does not support the definition’s first, descriptive statement about what skewness measures.

The packet does not define skewness as a measure of how unevenly values are distributed around the center of a dataset; it only mentions standardized scores of skewness in the context of testing normality.

The statement that skewness is used in research methods to check whether data follow a normal distribution is broader than the packet, which only says that skewness contributed to evidence that assumptions of normality were violated in one analysis.
